study_materials.objective: Build mastery of main idea and supporting evidence in Reading Comprehension.
study_materials.teaching_content: The main idea is the central point of a passage; supporting evidence includes details, examples, reasons or facts that develop that point.
worked_examples: If a passage explains how regular reading improves vocabulary and then gives several examples, the vocabulary benefit is the main idea and the examples are supporting evidence.
study_materials.pitfall: A vivid detail is not automatically the main idea.
study_materials.mastery_check: State the central idea and select details that directly support it.
study_materials.revision: Revise main idea and supporting evidence through examples, practice, correction and a final mastery check.

study_materials.objective: Build mastery of inference from explicit clues in Reading Comprehension.
study_materials.teaching_content: An inference is a reasonable conclusion supported by clues in the text rather than a sentence copied directly from it.
worked_examples: If a character carries an umbrella, wears a raincoat and avoids puddles, rain is a reasonable inference even if the passage never says 'it is raining.'
study_materials.pitfall: An inference must be supported by textual evidence, not personal imagination.
study_materials.mastery_check: Make inferences by combining explicit clues and rejecting unsupported assumptions.
study_materials.revision: Revise inference from explicit clues through examples, practice, correction and a final mastery check.

study_materials.objective: Build mastery of sequence cause and effect in Reading Comprehension.
study_materials.teaching_content: Sequence identifies the order of events; cause explains why something happens and effect describes what follows.
worked_examples: A storm causes a power cut, which then causes a computer to shut down: the storm is an earlier cause and the shutdown is a later effect.
study_materials.pitfall: The first event in a passage is not necessarily the cause of every later event.
study_materials.mastery_check: Trace chronological order and distinguish causes from consequences.
study_materials.revision: Revise sequence cause and effect through examples, practice, correction and a final mastery check.

study_materials.objective: Build mastery of author purpose and tone in Reading Comprehension.
study_materials.teaching_content: Author purpose describes why a text was written, such as to inform, explain, persuade or entertain. Tone describes the writer's attitude.
worked_examples: A notice giving exam timings mainly informs, while an advertisement encouraging readers to buy a product aims to persuade.
study_materials.pitfall: Purpose and tone are related but not identical.
study_materials.mastery_check: Identify purpose from content and tone from word choice and attitude.
study_materials.revision: Revise author purpose and tone through examples, practice, correction and a final mastery check.

study_materials.objective: Build mastery of fact opinion and interpretation in Reading Comprehension.
study_materials.teaching_content: A fact can be checked against evidence; an opinion expresses a judgment or belief; an interpretation explains meaning from available evidence.
worked_examples: 'The library opens at 9 a.m.' is checkable, while 'The library is the best place in town' is an opinion.
study_materials.pitfall: An opinion can sound confident without becoming a fact.
study_materials.mastery_check: Classify statements and justify the classification from the wording and evidence.
study_materials.revision: Revise fact opinion and interpretation through examples, practice, correction and a final mastery check.

study_materials.objective: Build mastery of context clues in Vocabulary.
study_materials.teaching_content: Context clues are nearby words or sentences that help determine an unfamiliar word's meaning.
worked_examples: In 'The glass was fragile, so it broke when dropped,' the consequence supplies a clue that fragile means easily broken.
study_materials.pitfall: Choosing the most familiar dictionary meaning can be wrong when context points to another sense.
study_materials.mastery_check: Infer word meaning using surrounding evidence before selecting an option.
study_materials.revision: Revise context clues through examples, practice, correction and a final mastery check.

study_materials.objective: Build mastery of synonyms and antonyms in Vocabulary.
study_materials.teaching_content: Synonyms have similar meanings and antonyms have contrasting meanings, but the relationship depends on context and part of speech.
worked_examples: 'Rapid' and 'swift' are close synonyms when describing movement; 'rapid' and 'slow' are contrasts.
study_materials.pitfall: Words that look related are not necessarily interchangeable in every sentence.
study_materials.mastery_check: Select a synonym or antonym that fits both meaning and grammatical use.
study_materials.revision: Revise synonyms and antonyms through examples, practice, correction and a final mastery check.

study_materials.objective: Build mastery of word families in Vocabulary.
study_materials.teaching_content: A word family contains related forms built around a common base, often changing part of speech or grammatical function.
worked_examples: Decide, decision and decisive share a base idea but serve different grammatical roles.
study_materials.pitfall: Related words can differ in meaning enough that replacing one with another changes the sentence.
study_materials.mastery_check: Use word-family relationships to infer meaning and choose the correct form.
study_materials.revision: Revise word families through examples, practice, correction and a final mastery check.

study_materials.objective: Build mastery of roots prefixes and suffixes in Vocabulary.
study_materials.teaching_content: Roots carry core meaning while prefixes and suffixes modify meaning or grammatical role.
worked_examples: 'Un-' can reverse meaning in words such as unhappy; '-less' can indicate absence, as in careless.
study_materials.pitfall: A prefix or suffix does not always give a complete definition without context.
study_materials.mastery_check: Break unfamiliar words into meaningful parts and test the resulting meaning against context.
study_materials.revision: Revise roots prefixes and suffixes through examples, practice, correction and a final mastery check.

study_materials.objective: Build mastery of precision in word choice in Vocabulary.
study_materials.teaching_content: Precise word choice selects the word that conveys the intended meaning, strength and tone most accurately.
worked_examples: 'Stroll' suggests a relaxed walk, while 'march' suggests purposeful movement; both relate to walking but are not interchangeable.
study_materials.pitfall: Using a broad synonym can remove an important distinction.
study_materials.mastery_check: Choose vocabulary based on meaning, context, intensity and tone.
study_materials.revision: Revise precision in word choice through examples, practice, correction and a final mastery check.

study_materials.objective: Build mastery of parts of speech in Grammar.
study_materials.teaching_content: Parts of speech describe grammatical roles such as noun, verb, adjective, adverb, pronoun, preposition and conjunction.
worked_examples: In 'The bright bird flew quickly,' bird is a noun, bright an adjective, flew a verb and quickly an adverb.
study_materials.pitfall: A word's part of speech can depend on how it functions in a sentence.
study_materials.mastery_check: Identify words by their function in the sentence, not by memorized appearance alone.
study_materials.revision: Revise parts of speech through examples, practice, correction and a final mastery check.

study_materials.objective: Build mastery of sentence structure in Grammar.
study_materials.teaching_content: A complete sentence normally expresses a complete thought and contains an appropriate subject and predicate; clauses can be independent or dependent.
worked_examples: 'Because the rain stopped' is dependent and incomplete by itself, while 'The match resumed' is an independent clause.
study_materials.pitfall: Adding a capital letter and full stop does not turn a fragment into a complete sentence.
study_materials.mastery_check: Identify sentence boundaries and distinguish complete clauses from fragments.
study_materials.revision: Revise sentence structure through examples, practice, correction and a final mastery check.

study_materials.objective: Build mastery of subject verb agreement in Grammar.
study_materials.teaching_content: The finite verb must agree with its subject in number and person.
worked_examples: 'The list of names is on the desk' uses is because list, not names, is the subject.
study_materials.pitfall: A nearby plural noun can distract from the true singular subject.
study_materials.mastery_check: Locate the grammatical subject before choosing the verb form.
study_materials.revision: Revise subject verb agreement through examples, practice, correction and a final mastery check.

study_materials.objective: Build mastery of verb tenses in Grammar.
study_materials.teaching_content: Verb tense locates an action in time and can show relationships between events.
worked_examples: 'She finished the work before the teacher arrived' uses past forms to show two completed events, with before establishing their order.
study_materials.pitfall: Changing tense without a reason can make time relationships unclear.
study_materials.mastery_check: Choose tense from the intended time reference and relationship between actions.
study_materials.revision: Revise verb tenses through examples, practice, correction and a final mastery check.

study_materials.objective: Build mastery of pronouns and modifiers in Grammar.
study_materials.teaching_content: Pronouns replace nouns; modifiers describe or limit words. Both should have clear references and logical placement.
worked_examples: In 'After reading the book, Maya wrote a review,' Maya is the person who read the book, so the modifier is logically attached.
study_materials.pitfall: A misplaced modifier can accidentally suggest that the wrong subject performed an action.
study_materials.mastery_check: Use clear pronoun references and place modifiers next to the words they logically describe.
study_materials.revision: Revise pronouns and modifiers through examples, practice, correction and a final mastery check.

study_materials.objective: Build mastery of punctuation in Usage & Editing.
study_materials.teaching_content: Punctuation marks clarify sentence boundaries, pauses, relationships and meaning.
worked_examples: 'Let's eat, Grandma' uses a comma to address Grandma; removing it changes the reading.
study_materials.pitfall: Do not insert commas merely wherever speech pauses.
study_materials.mastery_check: Choose punctuation from grammatical structure and intended meaning.
study_materials.revision: Revise punctuation through examples, practice, correction and a final mastery check.

study_materials.objective: Build mastery of capitalization in Usage & Editing.
study_materials.teaching_content: Capital letters begin sentences and proper nouns and appear in established uses such as titles and the pronoun I.
worked_examples: 'Monday' is capitalized because it names a day, while 'month' is normally lowercase generically.
study_materials.pitfall: Capitalizing a common noun does not make it a proper noun.
study_materials.mastery_check: Apply capitalization rules consistently.
study_materials.revision: Revise capitalization through examples, practice, correction and a final mastery check.

study_materials.objective: Build mastery of common usage errors in Usage & Editing.
study_materials.teaching_content: Common errors include agreement, homophones, tense consistency and faulty pronoun reference.
worked_examples: 'Their going to school' should be 'They're going to school'; their is possessive.
study_materials.pitfall: A word can sound right while being grammatically wrong.
study_materials.mastery_check: Identify the error and explain the context-appropriate correction.
study_materials.revision: Revise common usage errors through examples, practice, correction and a final mastery check.

study_materials.objective: Build mastery of sentence correction in Usage & Editing.
study_materials.teaching_content: Sentence correction checks grammar, meaning, agreement, tense, word choice and completeness.
worked_examples: 'Neither the teacher nor the students were ready' uses agreement with the nearer plural subject.
study_materials.pitfall: A correction that changes intended meaning is not successful.
study_materials.mastery_check: Make the smallest accurate correction while preserving meaning.
study_materials.revision: Revise sentence correction through examples, practice, correction and a final mastery check.

study_materials.objective: Build mastery of passage editing in Usage & Editing.
study_materials.teaching_content: Passage editing checks connected text for consistency, punctuation, spelling, grammar and clarity.
worked_examples: A passage can have individually correct sentences but inconsistent tense across sentences.
study_materials.pitfall: Editing is not rewriting every sentence.
study_materials.mastery_check: Edit systematically while preserving the intended message and voice.
study_materials.revision: Revise passage editing through examples, practice, correction and a final mastery check.

study_materials.objective: Build mastery of sentence construction in Writing Skills.
study_materials.teaching_content: Strong sentences have a clear subject, purposeful verb and relevant information.
worked_examples: 'The team practised after school because the final was near' combines a main clause and reason clause.
study_materials.pitfall: Longer sentences are not automatically better.
study_materials.mastery_check: Construct complete sentences and vary structure when useful.
study_materials.revision: Revise sentence construction through examples, practice, correction and a final mastery check.

study_materials.objective: Build mastery of paragraph organization in Writing Skills.
study_materials.teaching_content: A coherent paragraph develops one controlling idea through a topic sentence, relevant support and an appropriate close or transition.
worked_examples: A paragraph about healthy sleep can state importance, give two benefits and connect them to daily habits.
study_materials.pitfall: Unrelated facts do not form a coherent paragraph.
study_materials.mastery_check: Arrange ideas logically and keep details connected to the main point.
study_materials.revision: Revise paragraph organization through examples, practice, correction and a final mastery check.

study_materials.objective: Build mastery of descriptive writing in Writing Skills.
study_materials.teaching_content: Descriptive writing uses precise sensory details and carefully selected vocabulary to create a focused impression.
worked_examples: Instead of 'The market was nice,' mention bright signs, spice smells and vendors' voices.
study_materials.pitfall: Many adjectives without relevant detail can remain vague.
study_materials.mastery_check: Use specific sensory evidence and precise nouns and verbs.
study_materials.revision: Revise descriptive writing through examples, practice, correction and a final mastery check.

study_materials.objective: Build mastery of narrative writing in Writing Skills.
study_materials.teaching_content: Narrative writing presents connected events and may include characters, setting, conflict, actions and resolution.
worked_examples: A story can establish a lost notebook, show the search and resolve the problem when it is found.
study_materials.pitfall: A sequence without connection or purpose feels like a list.
study_materials.mastery_check: Build coherent sequence with cause-and-effect and resolution.
study_materials.revision: Revise narrative writing through examples, practice, correction and a final mastery check.

study_materials.objective: Build mastery of persuasive expression in Writing Skills.
study_materials.teaching_content: Persuasive writing states a position and supports it with reasons and evidence while considering the audience.
worked_examples: A recycling proposal can state the claim, give evidence, address convenience and propose action.
study_materials.pitfall: Persuasion is not repeated opinion or exaggerated language.
study_materials.mastery_check: State a clear claim and support it with relevant evidence and tone.
study_materials.revision: Revise persuasive expression through examples, practice, correction and a final mastery check.

study_materials.objective: Build mastery of character and setting in Literary Understanding.
study_materials.teaching_content: Character refers to people or beings in a story; setting establishes when and where events occur and can influence behaviour.
worked_examples: A character crossing a flooded village faces different choices from one in a safe city, showing setting's effect.
study_materials.pitfall: Setting includes time, atmosphere and social conditions, not only location.
study_materials.mastery_check: Use textual details to explain character and setting relationships.
study_materials.revision: Revise character and setting through examples, practice, correction and a final mastery check.

study_materials.objective: Build mastery of plot conflict and resolution in Literary Understanding.
study_materials.teaching_content: Plot is a sequence of connected events; conflict creates tension and resolution addresses the central problem.
worked_examples: Two friends disagree, face consequences and reconcile: interpersonal conflict drives later events.
study_materials.pitfall: The most dramatic event is not always the resolution.
study_materials.mastery_check: Trace the problem, turning points and outcome with evidence.
study_materials.revision: Revise plot conflict and resolution through examples, practice, correction and a final mastery check.

study_materials.objective: Build mastery of theme and message in Literary Understanding.
study_materials.teaching_content: Theme is a broader idea about life or experience developed by a text; a message communicates what the text suggests about it.
worked_examples: Repeated choices showing honesty despite difficulty may support a theme about integrity.
study_materials.pitfall: Theme should not be reduced to one plot detail.
study_materials.mastery_check: Infer theme from repeated patterns, choices, consequences and ending.
study_materials.revision: Revise theme and message through examples, practice, correction and a final mastery check.

study_materials.objective: Build mastery of figurative language in Literary Understanding.
study_materials.teaching_content: Figurative language communicates beyond literal meaning through devices such as simile, metaphor, personification and hyperbole.
worked_examples: 'The classroom was a zoo' is metaphor for disorder or noise, not literal animals.
study_materials.pitfall: Literal interpretation can obscure intended effect.
study_materials.mastery_check: Identify the device and explain its contextual effect.
study_materials.revision: Revise figurative language through examples, practice, correction and a final mastery check.

study_materials.objective: Build mastery of poetry interpretation in Literary Understanding.
study_materials.teaching_content: Poetry communicates through imagery, sound, rhythm, word choice, repetition, structure and figurative language.
worked_examples: Repeated darkness followed by morning may support an interpretation of difficulty followed by hope.
study_materials.pitfall: Interpretation must be grounded in the poem rather than personal association alone.
study_materials.mastery_check: Support interpretations with specific textual patterns.
study_materials.revision: Revise poetry interpretation through examples, practice, correction and a final mastery check.

study_materials.objective: Build mastery of functional texts in Communication.
study_materials.teaching_content: Functional texts serve practical purposes, including forms, schedules, emails, advertisements, menus and notices.
worked_examples: A timetable organizes times and locations so a reader can act quickly.
study_materials.pitfall: Reading a functional text like a story can hide key constraints.
study_materials.mastery_check: Extract purpose, key information, constraints and required action.
study_materials.revision: Revise functional texts through examples, practice, correction and a final mastery check.

study_materials.objective: Build mastery of instructions and notices in Communication.
study_materials.teaching_content: Instructions specify procedures; notices communicate information, rules, changes or warnings.
worked_examples: A laboratory notice may state a safety rule while instructions provide the procedure steps.
study_materials.pitfall: A notice does not necessarily contain every task step.
study_materials.mastery_check: Identify sequence, conditions, prohibitions and actions.
study_materials.revision: Revise instructions and notices through examples, practice, correction and a final mastery check.

study_materials.objective: Build mastery of formal and informal language in Communication.
study_materials.teaching_content: Formal language suits official, academic or professional contexts; informal language suits familiar conversation.
worked_examples: A request to a principal normally uses respectful formal register, unlike a message to a close friend.
study_materials.pitfall: Formal does not mean unnecessarily complicated.
study_materials.mastery_check: Match register to audience, purpose and situation.
study_materials.revision: Revise formal and informal language through examples, practice, correction and a final mastery check.

study_materials.objective: Build mastery of dialogue comprehension in Communication.
study_materials.teaching_content: Dialogue reveals information through words, responses and implied intentions.
worked_examples: Repeatedly avoiding a direct question can imply discomfort even without stating it.
study_materials.pitfall: Literal words may not reveal full conversational intention.
study_materials.mastery_check: Track speakers, explicit information, implied meaning and attitude.
study_materials.revision: Revise dialogue comprehension through examples, practice, correction and a final mastery check.

study_materials.objective: Build mastery of information synthesis in Communication.
study_materials.teaching_content: Synthesis combines relevant points from different parts or sources to form a supported conclusion.
worked_examples: A timetable gives event times and a notice gives eligibility; together they determine which event a student can attend.
study_materials.pitfall: Listing facts without explaining their relationship is not synthesis.
study_materials.mastery_check: Combine complementary evidence and state the supported conclusion.
study_materials.revision: Revise information synthesis through examples, practice, correction and a final mastery check.

study_materials.objective: Build mastery of analogy in Verbal Reasoning.
study_materials.teaching_content: An analogy compares relationships between pairs or groups of words; the relationship matters more than topic.
worked_examples: 'Bird : nest :: bee : hive' is animal to typical home.
study_materials.pitfall: Broad association is not the same as an equivalent relationship.
study_materials.mastery_check: Identify the precise first relationship before testing options.
study_materials.revision: Revise analogy through examples, practice, correction and a final mastery check.

study_materials.objective: Build mastery of classification in Verbal Reasoning.
study_materials.teaching_content: Classification groups items by a defining property or identifies an item that does not belong.
worked_examples: Apple, mango and banana can be fruits while carrot differs under that rule.
study_materials.pitfall: An item may fit multiple categories, so infer the intended rule from the set.
study_materials.mastery_check: State the rule and test every option against it.
study_materials.revision: Revise classification through examples, practice, correction and a final mastery check.

study_materials.objective: Build mastery of sentence completion in Verbal Reasoning.
study_materials.teaching_content: Sentence completion depends on grammar, meaning, logical relationships and context.
worked_examples: 'The road was flooded, so the match was ___' supports 'cancelled' or 'postponed' depending on options.
study_materials.pitfall: Grammatical fit alone is insufficient if meaning conflicts.
study_materials.mastery_check: Use grammar and contextual logic together.
study_materials.revision: Revise sentence completion through examples, practice, correction and a final mastery check.

study_materials.objective: Build mastery of word relationships in Verbal Reasoning.
study_materials.teaching_content: Word relationships include part-whole, category-member, function, degree, cause-effect and opposites.
worked_examples: 'Page : book' is part-to-whole; 'teacher : school' can be person-to-workplace.
study_materials.pitfall: Common association does not guarantee the same relationship.
study_materials.mastery_check: Name the relationship and preserve its direction.
study_materials.revision: Revise word relationships through examples, practice, correction and a final mastery check.

study_materials.objective: Build mastery of verbal puzzles in Verbal Reasoning.
study_materials.teaching_content: Verbal puzzles combine vocabulary, ordering, clues and logical constraints.
worked_examples: If A is before B and B before C, A-B-C follows even without a direct A-C clue.
study_materials.pitfall: Guessing before applying constraints causes errors.
study_materials.mastery_check: Extract every constraint and eliminate arrangements that violate any clue.
study_materials.revision: Revise verbal puzzles through examples, practice, correction and a final mastery check.

study_materials.objective: Build mastery of language challenge strategy in English Competition Mastery.
study_materials.teaching_content: Identify whether an English challenge tests comprehension, vocabulary, grammar, editing, literature, communication, or reasoning before selecting a method.
worked_examples: For a sentence-correction question, first identify whether the issue concerns agreement, tense, word choice, punctuation, or structure.
study_materials.pitfall: Pitfall: changing a sentence because it sounds unfamiliar without identifying a specific language rule.
study_materials.mastery_check: Classify the tested English skill and apply an evidence-based solving method.
study_materials.revision: Revise language challenge strategy through examples, practice, correction and a final mastery check.

study_materials.objective: Build mastery of contextual meaning reasoning in English Competition Mastery.
study_materials.teaching_content: Infer word and phrase meaning from surrounding sentences, tone, grammar, and textual evidence rather than relying only on the most familiar definition.
worked_examples: A word with several meanings should be interpreted using the sentence and paragraph that surround it.
study_materials.pitfall: Pitfall: selecting a dictionary meaning that conflicts with the passage context.
study_materials.mastery_check: Justify an interpretation using clear textual evidence.
study_materials.revision: Revise contextual meaning reasoning through examples, practice, correction and a final mastery check.

study_materials.objective: Build mastery of editing and error diagnosis in English Competition Mastery.
study_materials.teaching_content: Locate the first meaningful error in grammar, usage, punctuation, spelling, or sentence structure and explain the correction.
worked_examples: When a sentence contains a tense mismatch, identify the time reference and then correct the verb form consistently.
study_materials.pitfall: Pitfall: correcting style preferences when the actual problem is grammatical or usage-based.
study_materials.mastery_check: Identify, explain, and correct an English language error accurately.
study_materials.revision: Revise editing and error diagnosis through examples, practice, correction and a final mastery check.

study_materials.objective: Build mastery of integrated English challenges in English Competition Mastery.
study_materials.teaching_content: Combine reading, vocabulary, grammar, literary interpretation, writing, and verbal reasoning in unfamiliar formats.
worked_examples: A passage challenge may require identifying its main idea, interpreting a phrase, correcting an error, and selecting the strongest supporting sentence.
study_materials.pitfall: Pitfall: solving each clue independently when the passage provides connected evidence.
study_materials.mastery_check: Combine multiple English skills to solve an integrated challenge.
study_materials.revision: Revise integrated English challenges through examples, practice, correction and a final mastery check.

study_materials.objective: Build mastery of English championship round in English Competition Mastery.
study_materials.teaching_content: Practice timed mixed English challenges with careful reading, elimination, evidence checks, and final accuracy review.
worked_examples: Answer direct vocabulary and grammar questions first, then spend remaining time on longer comprehension and reasoning items.
study_materials.pitfall: Pitfall: choosing an answer from a familiar keyword without rereading the relevant context.
study_materials.mastery_check: Complete a mixed English challenge accurately under time pressure and justify difficult answers from language evidence.
study_materials.revision: Revise English championship round through examples, practice, correction and a final mastery check.

mock_tests.focus: writing, literature, communication and verbal reasoning
